sections.h2: Where is the Union County Recorder of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is in the Union County Courthouse at 103 South Second Street, Lewisburg, PA 17837, and the main number is (570) 524-8762. It shares space with the Register of Wills, and the same elected office covers both jobs. Counter hours run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., though the county notes that document recording concludes at 4:15 p.m.

That fifteen minute gap trips up closings. A deed brought in at 4:20 is not recorded that day, so a title agent or seller who needs same-day recording should plan to arrive well before the cutoff.

sections.h2: What does the Union County recorder do?
sections.html:
The office is responsible for recording documents tied to property: deeds, mortgages, releases, easements and rights of way, subdivisions and restrictions. It also records notary and county officer information and military service discharges. Records from January 1, 1962 to the present can be searched online, and anything earlier is on microfilm.

The recorder also collects the real estate transfer tax for the state, the townships, the boroughs and the school districts. That makes it the last stop in a sale: the buyer and seller sign at closing, then the deed is recorded here and the taxes are paid at the same time.

sections.h2: What are the recording rules for a deed in Union County?
sections.html:
The county publishes a short list of recording requirements, and a document that misses one comes back unrecorded. Mailed documents that cannot be recorded are returned with a letter of explanation and a $3.00 charge.

  • The acknowledgment must show the county, state, date, the people or corporate officers who appeared, and the notary's signature, seal and expiration date.
  • The notary stamp must be clear, and the stamp, seal and signature must not overlap one another.
  • Every deed, mortgage and mortgage assignment needs a signed certificate of address for the grantee, mortgagee or assignee.
  • A re-recorded document needs fresh acknowledgments and a note on why it is being filed again.
  • A Statement of Value, when one is required, must be filed in duplicate, fully completed, signed and dated.
  • Each recorded document and each transfer tax payment gets its own check, payable to Union County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Blanket documents are refused, and checks must be for the exact amount because no refunds are given.
  • Return by mail needs a stamped, self-addressed envelope supplied at the time of recording.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Union County?
sections.html:
The county posts a Recorder of Deeds fee schedule on its website under the Recorder pages, and the amount depends on the type of document, its page count and the number of names. Ask the office at (570) 524-8762 for the current total on your deed before you write the check, since checks must match the fee exactly.

Pennsylvania adds a 1 percent state realty transfer tax on the value of the property, and the Department of Revenue says buyer and seller share legal liability for it. The recorder remits the state portion, and local governments may share their own tax between municipalities and school districts. Exempt transfers include certain family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy.

sections.h2: What is Union County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Union County is one of the smallest counties in Pennsylvania, the fourth smallest by area, at 316 square miles of land. Wikipedia reports that it was created on March 22, 1813 from part of Northumberland County. Mifflinburg was the first county seat, New Berlin took over in 1815, and Lewisburg has held the role since 1855.

It is also far more densely settled than Somerset or Venango County, with 135.1 people per square mile in 2020 against 69.0 and 74.8 there. The county has four boroughs, Hartleton, Lewisburg, Mifflinburg and New Berlin, and its main roads include Interstate 80, US 15 and PA 45. In 2010 Lewisburg had 5,792 residents and Mifflinburg 3,540.

sections.h2: What should a seller bring to the Union County recorder?
sections.html:
Most sales are recorded by the title company, but a seller who handles the paperwork should assemble the signed and notarized deed, the certificate of address for the buyer, a Statement of Value when the tax is not paid in full, separate checks for the recording fee and for each tax payment, and a stamped return envelope. Having every item on this list in one folder is what keeps a closing from slipping a day.

  • Deed with a complete, legible notary block.
  • Signed certificate of address for the grantee.
  • Checks written to Union County Recorder of Deeds, one per document and per tax.
  • Statement of Value in duplicate, if it applies.

If you want to skip showings and repairs entirely, a direct cash sale of the house as it is can be arranged on your timeline, and the recording steps above are the same either way.

faqs.q: What time does the Union County recorder stop recording documents?
faqs.a: Recording concludes at 4:15 p.m., although the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. Anything that arrives after 4:15 waits for the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I record a Union County deed by mail?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope and the right checks. A document that cannot be recorded is returned with a letter of explanation and a $3.00 fee.

faqs.q: How far back do Union County online records go?
faqs.a: Records from January 1, 1962 to the present can be searched online. Earlier records were placed on microfilm and are available through the office.

faqs.q: Does the county accept one check for everything?
faqs.a: No. The recording requirements call for separate checks for each recorded document and for each realty transfer tax payment, all in the correct amount.

faqs.q: Who collects realty transfer tax in Union County?
faqs.a: The Recorder of Deeds collects it for the state, townships, boroughs and school districts. The state rate is 1 percent, and local shares are added by the municipalities and districts.
